subject: Renewal: increase reserved GPU pool and updated monthly commit — ScaleUp Analytics
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@scaleup.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning — reserved pool increase & monthly commit options

Hi Alyssa,

Quick note as we approach your contract renewal window (Jan 15): thanks again for the productive trial last quarter. Based on the usage telemetry and the request from your infra team, it sounds like doubling the reserved pool would be the lowest-friction path to hit your throughput targets for the ML inference pipelines.

High-level proposal I wanted to float before we draft an amendment:
- Move from the current 8-GPU reserved pool to a 16-GPU pool (same machine types).
- Updated monthly commit to reflect steady-state throughput — I’ve sketched two options (see below).
- Option A: 16 GPUs with a 6-month billing cadence, 10% discount off list.
- Option B: 16 GPUs with 12-month commit, 18% discount and 99.95% uptime SLA on the dedicated pool.

Questions for you: timeline for procurement/PO? Any internal approval cadence we should align with? Do you want us to include a short performance acceptance test (1 week of traffic with agreed pass criteria) as part of the amendment?

I’m happy to loop in contracts and your procurement counterpart once you’re comfortable with the approach. I’ll attach a draft scope if that helps.

Best,
Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192
[Attachment: draft_amendment_scope_v1.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@scaleup.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@scaleup.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — reserved pool increase & monthly commit options

Hi Kim,

Thanks — this aligns with where the team landed. A few clarifications:
1) We are comfortable moving to 16 GPUs but need a documented throughput guarantee (tokens/sec per GPU baseline) for our SRE to sign off.
2) Procurement timeline: we need a signed amendment and an order form by Jan 10 to hit our renewal target on Jan 15; finance will issue PO within 5 business days after that.
3) Preference is the 12-month commit (Option B) for budget predictability, but we need the SLA uplift and a clear break clause if usage drops below 55% for 2 consecutive months.

Can you include the acceptance test? One week of production-like traffic with agreed P95 latency target would be ideal. Also include any expected lead time for capacity transition — our ops folks want to know when the extra nodes will be live.

Alyssa
Head of Infrastructure
ScaleUp Analytics
alyssa@scaleup.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 08:26:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal planning — reserved pool increase & monthly commit options

Marcus/Neha — forwarding Alyssa's reply above. Key asks: 16 GPU pool on a 12-month commit, SLA at 99.95% and a throughput baseline documented (tokens/sec per GPU). They want a one-week acceptance run before we finalize and a break clause for underutilization (usage <55% for 2 months). Procurement needs signed docs by Jan 10.

Could you: 1) confirm the SLA wording and any standard break clause language we can offer, 2) provide an estimated timeline to provision the additional pool (lead time in business days), and 3) draft the acceptance test criteria we should propose?

I'll keep the customer looped.

Thanks,
Kim

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal planning — reserved pool increase & monthly commit options

On Thu, Dec 17, 2026 at 08:26 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marcus/Neha — forwarding Alyssa's reply above.

Kim — we can support this. Notes:
- SLA: we can offer 99.95% uptime on the reserved pool for a 12-mo commit. Suggest adding standard remedies: service credits tiered by downtime exceeding SLA. Exclusion clauses for force majeure and planned maintenance windows (we usually give 72-hour advance notice for major infra work).
- Throughput baseline: we typically define a baseline in terms of p50/p95 tokens/sec for the model family and sequence length. For their usage pattern (avg seq len ~128, model: redwood-medium-XXL), we expect ~1.2k tokens/sec per V100-equivalent GPU at p50, ~950 tokens/sec p95. I'll convert to the exact units and include a 10% performance buffer.
- Provisioning lead time: 5 business days to expand the dedicated pool to 16 GPUs, assuming no hardware constraints. If they want specific machine type or zone pinning, add 3 days.
- Acceptance test: 7-day window, run production-like traffic (shared test token) with pass criteria: p95 latency < 240ms, error rate < 0.5%, and sustained throughput within 90% of expected baseline. Failure path: if not met, we rollback pricing for first month and provide 100% credit for that period.

I can draft the SLA and acceptance language for the amendment.

Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineering, Redwood
marcus@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@scaleup.ai>, procurement@scaleup.ai
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed amendment & order form — ScaleUp Analytics (16 GPU reserved pool)

Hi Alyssa,

Attached are the draft amendment and order form per our conversation:
- Amendment_Scope_ScaleUp.pdf — includes SLA language, throughput baseline, acceptance test criteria, and the underutilization break clause (usage <55% for two months triggers review and potential pro-rated reduction).
- OrderForm_ScaleUp_2027.pdf — reflects the 12-month commit pricing (18% discount) and updated monthly commit figures.

Summary of key commercial terms:
- Transition: 8 -> 16 GPUs (same instance family).
- Commit: 12 months, billed monthly.
- Pricing: 18% committed discount over hosted list.
- SLA: 99.95% uptime on reserved pool.
- Acceptance: 7-day production-style test; pass criteria p95 latency <240ms, error rate <0.5%.
- Lead time: 5 business days to provision after signed amendment + PO.

If that looks good, please sign the order form and send PO by Jan 10. If you prefer, we can also do DocuSign — I included a link to the hosted quote.

Best,
Kim

[Attachments: Amendment_Scope_ScaleUp.pdf (PDF, 64KB); OrderForm_ScaleUp_2027.pdf (PDF, 22KB)]
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@scaleup.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@scaleup.ai, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed amendment & order form — ScaleUp Analytics (16 GPU reserved pool)

Kim,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear terms — this is mostly aligned. A couple of small asks from Finance & SRE before we sign:
1) Add a 30-day notice to the underutilization clause to allow us to produce usage reports before any action is taken.
2) Can you confirm whether the acceptance test will run on the same physical hardware as the production pool or on a mirrored staging pool? Our legal prefers staging if possible.

If you confirm those two items I’ll route to Finance for the PO. We may take DocuSign.

Thanks,
Alyssa
